enrichment.headline: Buys Titan School Solutions software to manage the nutrition program, up to $169,357 through 2021
enrichment.summary: The district is buying Titan School Solutions software to manage its student meal program, for up to $169,356.95 over the whole term. That is up to $62,378 through June 2020 and up to $106,978.95 for July 2020 through June 2021. The term started in November 2019, before this approval.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Titan School Solutions - Nutrition Program Management Software - Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Hires Hazelrigg to handle workers' compensation claims for up to $2.09M over three years
enrichment.summary: Hazelrigg Claims Management Service, an outside claims administrator in Chino Hills, will review and manage the district's workers' compensation claims from July 2020 through June 2023. Fees are capped at $2,090,772 in total, with yearly caps of $669,760, $696,550 and $724,412. The contract also allows two one-year renewals.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Professional Services Contract – District and Hazelrigg Claims Management Service - Workers’ Compensations Claims - Risk Management Department

enrichment.headline: Moves the milk and dairy supply contract to Crystal Creamery, up to $250,000, after Berkeley Farms closed
enrichment.summary: The district's milk and dairy bid award moves from Berkeley Farms Dairy, which stopped operating, to Crystal Creamery of Modesto, the second-lowest responsive bidder. Crystal Creamery will deliver milk and dairy products for the rest of the 2019-20 school year, up to $250,000, with two one-year renewal options. The Superintendent's earlier action is also being ratified.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Transfer - Award of Bid - Milk/Dairy Products - RFP/Bid No. 19-01 - Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Accepts $97,500 from No Kid Hungry to support meal distribution during COVID-19
enrichment.summary: The No Kid Hungry Campaign is giving the district $97,500 to help run its Grab and Go meal distribution for children and families during the COVID-19 emergency. The grant covers March 16 through June 30, 2020.

items.fundingSource: Grant Award - No Kid Hungry Campaign

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Grant Award – No Kid Hungry Campaign – COVID-19 Emergency – Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Renews no-cost partnership with Center for Ecoliteracy on school food, 2020-2023
